title: Grateful Dead Live at Winterland Arena on 1967-10-22

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy 1967 show highlighted by a smoking Cryptical / Other One and fiery New Potato/Caboose performances
ai_review.review: The recording is a pristine soundboard source that sounds great for its era, with every instrument clear and well balanced. The concert itself is tight and energetic – the band plays together without sloppiness, delivering standout renditions of Cryptical/Other One, Lovelight, New Potato Caboose and Beat It, while Jerry’s guitar work is described as volcanic and passionately vicious.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high star ratings (mostly 5s) and enthusiastic comments about both performance and sound quality indicate a strong show with an excellent soundboard recording.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Great, clear sound for its age; all instruments audible, crisp mix, no major drop‑outs noted.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Tightly knit set with seamless transitions, especially the Cryptical‑Other One pairing; the band stays together throughout, delivering a polished, high‑energy performance.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s playing is described as “brutal viciousness,” “sweet passion,” “magma discharge,” and consistently fiery throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh provides strong counter‑point to Jerry, with notable bass work that follows Jerry’s lead; praised for his tight interplay.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir is noted as solid on Beat It, delivering good rhythm guitar and vocals.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann holds the groove solo early in the night; later reviewers note Bill and Mickey Hart working smoothly together.
